name: python-repo-symbol-not-imported-asks
desc: `render` is a real symbol in app/render.py but the edited test file neither imports nor defines it — the 'real symbol, wrong scope' class the additive check structurally cannot see (it resolves repo-wide, so `render` is known and stays silent). enrolled_defs pins that `render` really is in the repo index, which is the firewall precondition: without it the check would abstain rather than fire. Write-shaped, so it also covers the whole-file-content replay path
new:
import pytest


def test_digest():
    out = render(digest)
    assert out

name: python-symbol-imported-in-scope-clean
desc: same symbol, same call, but the edit imports it — correct usage stays silent. The highest-value case in this file by mutation score: it is the only fixture that fails if the in-file scope check, the fold of the edit's own bindings, or the import-binding rule is removed. enrolled_defs pins render as reachable, so this silence is a rule dropping a live candidate rather than an enrollment that resolved nothing
new:
import pytest

from app.render import render


def test_digest():
    out = render(digest)
    assert out

name: python-hunk-scoped-out-of-scope-asks
desc: the CONTROL for the two whole-file abstain fixtures below: an Edit whose hunk is byte-identical to theirs, against a file carrying no abstain marker → ask. Replayed as an Edit, not a Write, so the added-lines set is the hunk ALONE. That is what makes the pairing meaningful: the abstain cases differ from this one only in the pre-edit file's text, so their silence is attributable to the whole-file read rather than to anything in the added text

name: python-star-import-abstains-clean
desc: `from app.render import *` binds an unknowable set, so the whole file abstains even though `render` is bare-called and is a repo symbol. The star import sits OUTSIDE the edited hunk, so only the pre-edit file read carries it — delete the wholeFile arm of the abstain and this fixture asks, matching its control above. This is the load-bearing false-positive gate: a miss is free, a false alarm is the adoption-killer

name: python-dynamic-binding-abstains-clean
desc: a `globals().update(...)` elsewhere in the file can introduce any name at runtime, so no static scan can enumerate the binding surface and the file abstains. Same whole-file-only placement as the star-import case, but through the pyDynamicBinding marker list rather than the star-import regex — and `globals` itself is a Python builtin, so the additive check has nothing to say about it either

name: python-star-import-added-by-the-edit-abstains-clean
desc: the mirror of the two cases above: here the star import is introduced BY the hunk and the pre-edit file is clean, so only the added-text arm of the abstain can see it. Together with them, both arms of `abstainsFileScope(wholeFile) || abstainsFileScope(addedLines)` are independently pinned — remove either one and exactly one side of the pair fails

name: python-new-file-no-whole-file-context-clean
desc: a Write creating a file that does not exist yet: there is no pre-edit content, so the file's imports and definitions are unknowable and every reference would read as unresolved. The check must fail silent, matching the guard's degraded-input posture everywhere else. Pins the no-whole-file-context bail — remove it and this fixture flags `render` on a brand-new file, which is the worst false positive the surface could produce. Note the distinction the harness enforces: an existing EMPTY file still yields one blank line and the check does run, so only a genuinely missing file exercises the bail

name: python-firewall-leaves-invented-symbols-alone
desc: the firewall: file-scope considers ONLY names already in the repo index. `frobnicate` is in no file (enrolled_defs pins 0), so it is an invented symbol and belongs to the always-on additive check — which asks about it with the gate off. ask_without_flag inverts the isolation probe for this: what is pinned is that turning file-scope ON leaves the message byte-identical. Remove the firewall and the same name is reported twice, which no ask/no-ask assertion could ever see. This is the property that keeps the two checks disjoint and stops file-scope from widening the invented-symbol surface
